title: Astrocyte-mediated mitochondrial handling in retinal ganglion cell injury: from damaged cargo clearance to neuroinflammatory regulation and recovery responses
title_zh: 视网膜神经节细胞损伤中的星形胶质细胞介导的线粒体处理：从受损货物清除到神经炎症调节与恢复反应
abstract: Abstract Retinal ganglion cell (RGC) injury is a major feature of optic neuropathies and retinal degenerative diseases and is frequently accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, abnormal axonal transport, and impaired mitochondrial quality control. These abnormalities are often considered primarily in the context of the intrinsic vulnerability of RGCs, which have high energetic demands and long axonal projections. RGC axons, however, are situated within a specialized glial–vascular and metabolic environment in the retinal nerve fiber layer and optic nerve head, where astrocytes, vascular structures, extracellular matrix, and local metabolic conditions contribute to neuronal homeostasis. Mitochondrial injury in RGCs therefore also needs to be considered in relation to what happens to mitochondrial material once it extends beyond cell-autonomous quality control. Here, we examine mitochondrial fate at the astrocyte–RGC interface, with particular attention to the disposal of damaged mitochondrial material, its subsequent processing within astrocytes, and its potential involvement in neuroinflammatory regulation and tissue adaptation. Mitochondrial material released from injured RGC axons can be taken up by neighboring astrocytes, where it undergoes acidification and lysosome-associated processing. If this processing capacity becomes insufficient, persistent mitochondrial components such as mtDNA may contribute to inflammatory signaling and cellular stress. In the opposite direction, functional donor mitochondria can support stressed neurons or RGC-like cells under defined experimental conditions. Together, these observations extend the study of RGC mitochondrial injury beyond the neuron itself and place astrocytic processing, mitochondrial quality control, inflammatory regulation, and metabolic adaptation within the local astrocyte–RGC interface during optic nerve injury.
abstract_zh: 摘要 视网膜神经节细胞（RGC）损伤是视神经病变和视网膜退行性疾病的主要特征，常伴随线粒体功能障碍、氧化应激、轴突运输异常和线粒体质量控制受损。这些异常往往被视为RGC本身的内在脆弱性所致，因其能量需求高且轴突投射长。然而，RGC轴突位于视网膜神经纤维层和视神经头的专门胶质-血管及代谢环境中，星形胶质细胞、血管结构、细胞外基质和局部代谢条件共同维持神经元稳态。因此，RGC线粒体损伤也需要考虑线粒体物质在超出细胞自我质量控制后会发生什么。本文考察了星形胶质细胞与RGC界面处线粒体的命运，重点关注受损线粒体物质的处置、随后在星形胶质细胞内的处理以及其在神经炎症调节和组织适应中的潜在作用。受损RGC轴突释放的线粒体物质可被邻近星形胶质细胞摄取，在那里经历酸化和溶酶体相关处理。如果处理能力不足，持续存在的线粒体组分如mtDNA可能促成炎症信号和细胞应激。相反，在特定实验条件下，功能性供体线粒体可支持受压神经元或类似RGC的细胞。综上所述，这些观察将RGC线粒体损伤研究从单纯的神经元层面扩展到星形胶质细胞处理、线粒体质量控制、炎症调节和代谢适应，并将其置于视神经损伤期间的局部星形胶质细胞–RGC界面中。
